# native-attribution fixtures (SMI-6684 Wave 3)

Fixture data for `scripts/tests/check-native-modules-attribution.test.ts`, which
drives the REAL `scripts/lib/check-native-modules.sh` end to end through
PATH-injected fakes (`scripts/tests/check-native-modules-attribution.harness.ts`,
following the `scripts/tests/_lib/check-container-deps-fresh-fixtures.sh`
precedent). Each `cases/<CASE-ID>/` directory holds the checker-output
fixtures for one row of the 42-case table plus a handful of mechanism-only IDs
used by the harness's I-*/T-*/U-* scenarios. The design these cases come from
is recorded in `docs/internal/implementation/smi-6684-verification-surface-integrity.md`
§ Wave 3.

**Two prefixes, two namespaces — do not read one as the other.** A case-id
prefix (`R-`, `S-`, `T-`, `U-`, `M-`, `N-`, `A-`) names which row of the case
table it is; a *file* prefix names where the bytes came from. `R-meta-trunc`
is an `R-` case whose files are `synthetic-*`, and that is not a contradiction:
only the file prefix asserts provenance.

Every filename is prefixed with its **provenance** — never inferred, always
in the name:

| Prefix | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `real-` | A byte-for-byte capture from a real container, host path normalised (see below). |
| `real-paired-` | Two real captures (different times or containers) whose counts agree, used together as one case. |
| `derived-` | Computed *mechanically* from a real capture — see `generate-fixtures.mjs`. |
| `synthetic-` | Hand-built; never observed live. |

The harness strips the provenance prefix when it stages a case (e.g.
`real-paired-report` -> `report`) before pointing the fake checker's
`FAKE_CASE_DIR` at it, so the fake checker script itself (generated by the
harness, not committed here) stays an unmodified port of the verified
prototype (`report`, `report-tmp`, `stdout`, `rc`, `nonl`, `sleep`).

**Host-path normalisation**: the capturing machine's checkout path is replaced
in every real and derived file. The absolute form becomes `/HOST/skillsmith`,
the JSON reports' `scope_host_path` form becomes
`/HOST-noleadingslash/skillsmith`, and the `report_key` slug becomes
`HOST-skillsmith`. The classifier reads none of these fields, so the change
cannot alter a classification; it keeps an operator's home directory out of
committed fixtures.

## Regenerating

```
node scripts/tests/fixtures/native-attribution/generate-fixtures.mjs
```

Regenerates the 3 `derived-*` files from their `real-*`/`real-paired-*`
siblings, byte-for-byte, idempotently. It does **not** touch `synthetic-*`
files — a synthetic fixture has no real capture to derive it from (that is
what "synthetic" means here), so those are committed as their own source of
truth, hand-authored to match the FAIL-line and JSON-report shapes the real
checker (`scripts/lib/check-mount-composition.sh` /
`check-mount-composition.probes.sh`) actually produces.

## Provenance per case

| Case | Files | Provenance / origin |
|---|---|---|
| `R-main-degraded` | `real-paired-report`, `real-paired-stdout` | `report-main-degraded-2026-09-16T00-09Z.json` + `skillsmith-dev-1.out` (main checkout, 2026-09-16 captures) |
| `R-wt-degraded` | `real-stdout`, `derived-report` | stdout = `smi-6676-handle-relative-removal-spike-dev-1.out`; report computed from it (`generate-fixtures.mjs`) |
| `R-wt-floor` | `real-paired-report`, `real-paired-stdout` | `report-worktree-floor-2026-09-16T00-59Z.json` + `smi-6651-registry-content-release-rpc-dev-1.out` |
| `R-timeout-partial` | `real-stdout`, `synthetic-rc`, `synthetic-report-tmp` | stdout = `smi-6684-wire-mount-composition-detector-dev-1.out` (890B, rc=124); `rc`/`report-tmp` hand-built to complete the scenario |
| `T-partial-evidence` | `derived-stdout`, `synthetic-rc` | stdout = first 40 lines of `R-wt-degraded`'s real-stdout (`generate-fixtures.mjs`); `rc`=124 hand-set |
| `T-partial-lastline` | `derived-stdout`, `synthetic-nonl`, `synthetic-rc` | stdout = `R-timeout-partial`'s real-stdout, copied verbatim (`generate-fixtures.mjs`); the no-trailing-newline final line and rc are hand-built |
| `N-norep` | `synthetic-stdout` | the literal early-exit line `scripts/lib/check-mount-composition.sh:157`'s `fail A1 "no compose file..."` call produces, hand-reconstructed from checker SOURCE (not derived from a `real-*` capture) with the real `root=/app` argument -- provenance-labeled `synthetic-` per this file's own prefix rule (SMI-6684 Wave 3 review F-16b) |
| `R-meta-trunc` | `synthetic-report`, `synthetic-stdout` | Hand-built for the byte-level truncation lever: a single `missing_destinations` entry at a real tier-1 ancestor, so a cut final line would fabricate evidence if the guard regressed. **Fully synthetic despite the `R-` case id** — see the note below |
| `S-subst-main` | `synthetic-report`, `synthetic-stdout` | `S-subst-wt`'s pair with only `"mode"` changed to `"main"`, so the main-checkout MOUNT-SUBSTITUTED remedy line has a covering case. Added by the pre-merge gate's F-4 |
| `S-*`, `T-complete-*`, `T-host-watchdog`, `U-*`, `M-*`, `N-disable-*`, `A-unavailable` | `synthetic-*` (or no files, for the mechanism-only IDs `U-docker125`/`U-nonode`/`U-notimeout`/`A-unavailable`, which are driven entirely by harness env vars / PATH variants) | Hand-built to the cause-kind shapes the real checker produces; never observed live |

The expected `(state, reason, cause, tier, evidence)` for every case is
asserted by `scripts/tests/check-native-modules-attribution.test.ts`, which is
the authority. It is not restated here, and no uncommitted document is cited:
a fixture manifest that points at a file nobody can open is worse than one
that points at the test.
